name: Ghost
note: States on its own site that it doesn't test on animals and that its fragrances are Vegan Society approved. A rare case of a high-street name being both.

name: Lush
note: Long-standing anti-testing campaigner, and much of the range is vegan, though not all of it. Doesn't sell in mainland China.

name: Floral Street
note: British, vegan across the range, and the packaging is one of the few genuinely low-waste efforts in fragrance.

name: Stella McCartney
note: Cruelty-free, and the wider brand has been vocally anti-fur and anti-leather for years, though not every fragrance is confirmed vegan.

name: The 7 Virtues
note: Cruelty-free, and sources some of its ingredients from countries rebuilding after conflict.

name: Pacifica
note: Entirely vegan and cruelty-free, and one of the cheaper ways in.

name: Dossier
note: Makes affordable versions of well-known scents. Cruelty-free, and a good answer if there's a designer perfume you like but not who makes it.

name: Henry Rose
note: Cruelty-free, and unusually it publishes its full ingredient list rather than hiding behind the word "fragrance".

name: Skylar
note: Vegan and cruelty-free, built around lighter scents for people who find most perfume overwhelming.

name: Maison Louis Marie
note: Cruelty-free, and the oil-based versions are worth knowing about if alcohol-heavy sprays bother you.

name: Chanel
note: Sold in mainland China, where animal testing is still required for a lot of imported cosmetics. Chanel's own policy also allows for testing carried out by ingredient suppliers.

name: Lancome
note: Owned by L'Oreal, which also tests. Lancome's policy says it doesn't test "except when required by law", and it sells in mainland China, which is exactly where that exception applies.

name: Gucci
note: The fragrances are made under licence by Coty, not by Gucci itself, and PETA lists Gucci Fragrances (Coty) as testing on animals. A good example of why the name on the bottle isn't the thing to check.

name: Le Labo
note: Was widely recommended in cruelty-free circles until it opened stores in mainland China. Worth knowing if you bought it on an older recommendation.

name: Ariana Grande
note: Made under licence by Luxe Brands rather than by Ariana Grande directly, and I haven't been able to confirm that company's testing policy from a source I'd stand behind. Listed here rather than left out, because a lot of people ask about it.
